ledger.note: 1946: the State of East Indonesia is established on 24 December at the end of the Denpasar Conference (18-24 December) as a Dutch puppet state; 'It comprised every island to the east of Borneo'. The Dutch organised the Malino Conference in July 1946 for a federal USI (USI page).
1946: 'renamed on 27 December' (the page; from the Great East to the State of East Indonesia).

The Republic of South Maluku was proclaimed at Ambon on 25 April 1950 (RMS page); the State of East Indonesia page puts it 'after the cabinet formed in May 1950' and says the Moluccan rebellion was crushed in November 1950. [Reviewer se-04-x: confidence 3 to 2; the RMS page names 'the islands of Ambon, Buru, and Seram', not the whole of Maluku province.]

notes: State Cliopatria lacks, added by se-04-x. Dutch puppet state 1946-1948 and constituent state of the USI 1949-1950 (infobox); the dutch-east-indies dossier does not record it. Other Dutch-sponsored states, from the USI page (created; dissolved): East Sumatra (25 December 1947; 17 August 1950), Madura (20 February 1948; 9 March 1950), Pasundan (25 February 1948; 11 March 1950), South Sumatra (2 September 1948; 24 March 1950), East Java (27 November 1948; 9 March 1950), Central Java (2 March 1949; 9 March 1950), West Borneo (12 May 1947; 22 April 1950), East Borneo (12 May 1947; 24 March 1950), Great Dayak (3 June 1947; 4 April 1950), Bandjar (14 January 1948; 4 April 1950), Southeast Borneo Federation (March 1947; 4 April 1950), Bangka, Belitung and Riau (July 1947; 4 April 1950), Djakarta Federal District (June 1948; 11 March 1950): none written; Pasundan, East Java, East Sumatra, South Sumatra and West Borneo are the largest. The republic-of-indonesia dossier treats the USI of 27 December 1949 as a rename of the Republic (one state), so the USI is not a separate dossier; the SEI's join with the federation on 27 December 1949 has no ledger event. Leaders on the infobox: Tjokorda Gde Raka Soekawati (1946-1950), Nadjamuddin Daeng Malewa (first, 1946), Martinus Putuhena (last, 1950); no ruler strip. The South Moluccas proclamation: 25 April 1950 on the RMS page, 'after the cabinet formed in May 1950' on the SEI page. Page budget: 2 pages.
